quests.title: The Window Above Randwick
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. I live above the platform at Randwick and I know this line by sound. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Something in the rhythm changed about a month ago and everyone I tell thinks I am mad. Ride it and tell me whether I am mad. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

steps.label: ride it and listen to the joins
photograph the stretch that sounds wrong
tell me I am not mad

quests.title: Setting Up at Marayong
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. Five in the morning at Marayong, in the dark, unloading a van by feel. You will see what I mean the second you get there. The bloke in the next bay has started arriving at four to take half my frontage. I need a witness and I need them at four. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

steps.label: the bays, at the hour it happens
the bloke with the extra trestle
you will want one at that hour
$26 of frontage, recovered

quests.title: The Clock at Loftus
quests.blurb: The council knows and the council does not care. The clock on the Loftus platform has been four minutes fast since I got here and every relief who comes through wants to fix it. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. Do not fix it. Find out who set it that way, before they retire. Do that and we're square.

steps.label: the clock, four minutes fast, for the file
to Sutherland, where the old crew drink
bring the name back

quests.title: The Dog at The Star
quests.blurb: It has been three weeks. A dog meets the 5:40 at The Star every weekday and nobody gets off for it. It started small, the way these things do. Four months of this. I have decided it is not going to be a sad story. Find out whose it is. Ask for me by name at the counter.

steps.label: the end of the platform, at twenty to six
the collar, if it has got one
the street it walks home to
tell me it is not a sad story

quests.title: The Book at Marrickville
quests.blurb: Before you say anything: yes, I know. I run a small book on things that are not races — weather, delays, whether the the second express out of Marrickville runs on time. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. Somebody is beating it by information, not luck. Ride the run they ride. Do not let them talk you into anything.

steps.label: ride the run they ride
the two who follow you off it
$35 back off the book

quests.title: Last Service out of Mount Kuring-gai
quests.blurb: It is not a police matter and I have checked. The last one through Mount Kuring-gai carries four people and one of them is always asleep. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Ride it to Mount Colah, photograph the platform with nobody on it, and come back and tell me the place still exists when there is no one in it. There's cash in it. Not a lot.

steps.label: ride the late one to Mount Colah
the empty platform, lit and pointless
tell them what you saw

quests.title: The Arlington Tap-Off
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. Somebody taps on at Arlington at half six and never taps off. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Same card, 22 months running. Ride the run they ride and find where a person gets off this network without a gate seeing them. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

steps.label: ride the run the card rides
the gap in the fence everyone knows about
photograph it before somebody welds it

quests.title: The Gosford Order
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. Two hundred coffees out of Gosford before ten past five and I know every one of them by the walk. You will see what I mean the second you get there. The woman who runs the newsagent stopped coming three weeks back. Take one over to where they work and find out whether I lost them to the chain up the road. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

steps.label: order one at the Gosford kiosk
the office they walk to, or used to
come back with $30 — I am not running a charity

quests.title: Four Minutes at Childrens Hospital
quests.blurb: Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. The board at Childrens Hospital says four minutes. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. It has said four minutes since before the merge and it is a lie about a third of the time. Stand under it, time it, and bring me numbers instead of feelings. You'll know it when you see it.

steps.label: stand under the board and wait like everyone else
photograph the board saying four minutes
ride the one that finally comes
give me the number

quests.title: Unclaimed at Como
quests.blurb: Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. Everything anyone leaves on the Como line ends up in a room and the room is full. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. Nine hundred umbrellas and one a tallboy of something warm with a name on it and a number that rings out. Go to the address on the tag. You'll know it when you see it.

steps.label: the address on the tag
the two who got there before you
$35 — whatever it is, it is worth that to somebody

quests.title: The Quiet Carriage, Wentworth Park
quests.blurb: I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. The quiet carriage runs on shame and somebody on the quarter to six out of Wentworth Park has stopped feeling it. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Ride it, see the crime, and apply the shame manually. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.

steps.label: ride the quiet carriage and observe the crime
apply the shame manually
photograph the sign, for the record

quests.title: The Circular Quay Shortcut
quests.blurb: It is not a police matter and I have checked. Every courier has a route that is not on a map and mine goes through Circular Quay. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. They have started locking one end. Go and find out whether it is locked forever or just locked today. There's cash in it. Not a lot.

steps.label: the end they lock
the long way round, so you understand what it costs
$39, which is what the long way costs me a week

quests.title: Possession at Convention
quests.blurb: Before you say anything: yes, I know. We own the track between midnight and four and in that window we are the only people in this city doing anything real. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. Somebody keeps walking through my possession at Convention. Find them before a grinder does. Do not let them talk you into anything.

steps.label: where they come through the fence
the ones who think a hard hat is a costume
photograph the gap so I can put a number on the form

quests.title: The Kingsgrove Regular
quests.blurb: Before you say anything: yes, I know. A man drank in my front bar by Kingsgrove for 16 years and then stopped, and every regular in here has gone vague on me at once, which means they know. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. You are not from here. Go and knock. Do not let them talk you into anything.

steps.label: the house they say he moved to
you cannot ask a favour empty-handed
come back and tell me straight

quests.title: Bay 14, Lilyfield
quests.blurb: Nobody else has offered, so. Two hundred bays at Lilyfield and I have counted two hundred and forty cars in here on the long weekend. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. One of them has not moved since March and it has a ticket on it from March. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: the car, and the ticket, and the date on it
the two arguing over the grass
$32 in fines nobody is going to collect

quests.title: Whatever Is Under the Grey at Canterbury
quests.blurb: The council knows and the council does not care. Council pays me to paint over things and last week I painted over something good. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. There is another one near Canterbury that I am scheduled to kill on grand final week. Photograph it first. Do that and we're square.

steps.label: the wall, before they get to it
photograph it properly, not a phone-in-a-hurry job
show me

quests.title: The Hill Above Guildford
quests.blurb: Nobody else has offered, so. I drive past the same view above Guildford eleven times a shift and I have never once stopped at it. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. You have got legs and no timetable. Go up and photograph what I have been driving past for 21 years. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: up the hill, the way the road does not go
the view I have never stopped for
$30, because I am paying you for it

quests.title: Contesting It at Casula
quests.blurb: Nobody else has offered, so. Two hundred and eighty-five dollars at Casula for a thing the sign did not say, because the sign is not there. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. The form wants evidence. Go and photograph the absence. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: where the sign is supposed to be
photograph the absence, which is harder than it sounds
the one who tells you photography is not allowed here

quests.title: The Strip Outside Berowra
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. A metre of dirt between the fence and the footpath at Berowra, dead for 25 years and not dead now. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Council mows on the fifteenth and does not know what is in it. Stand near it and stop the man with the whipper snipper. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

steps.label: the strip, which is a garden now
the man with the whipper snipper
photograph it while it still exists

the loading door nobody watches
whoever is standing in it at two in the morning

quests.title: The Dog at Emu Plains

quests.title: The Book at Schofields
